spots.name: Gur-e-Amir
spots.summary: The Gur-e-Amir, also transcribed Gūr-i Amīr or Guri Amir is a mausoleum of the Turco-Mongol conqueror Timur in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.

spots.name: Registan
spots.summary: Registan, officially the Registan Square is a historic public square in the city of Samarkand, Uzbekistan. It served as the heart of the Timurid Empire and later as the city's commercial, educational, and ceremonial center.

spots.name: Shah-i-Zinda
spots.summary: Shah-i-Zinda is a necropolis in the north-eastern part of Samarkand, Uzbekistan.

spots.name: Bibi-Khanym Mosque
spots.summary: The Bibi-Khanym Mosque is one of the most important monuments of Samarkand, Uzbekistan. In the 15th century, it was one of the largest and most magnificent mosques in the Islamic world. It is considered a masterpiece of the Timurid Renaissance.

spots.name: Ulugh Beg Observatory
spots.summary: The Ulugh Beg Observatory is an observatory in modern day Samarkand, Uzbekistan, which was built in the 1420s by the Timurid astronomer Ulugh Beg. This school of astronomy was constructed under the Timurid Empire, and was the last of its kind from the Islamic Medieval period.

spots.name: Hazrat Khizr Mosque
spots.summary: The Hazrat Khizr Mosque is a historical monument in Samarkand, Uzbekistan ; associated with the name of the legendary Islamic prophet Khizr. The building was erected on the site of an ancient mosque. The monument is located opposite the Shah-i-Zinda complex on a hill.

spots.name: Afrasiab Museum of Samarkand
spots.summary: The Afrasiab Museum of Samarkand is a museum located at the historical site of Afrasiyab, one of the largest archaeological sites in the world and an ancient city that was destroyed by the Mongols in the early 13th century.

spots.name: Qusam Ibn Abbas Complex
spots.summary: Qusam Ibn Abbas Complex – an architectural monument in Samarkand as a part of Shah-i-Zinda. The complex consists of a mosque, a mausoleum and a shrine built in different periods. It was built around the tomb of Qutham ibn Abbas.

spots.name: St. John the Baptist Church, Samarkand

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The St. John the Baptist Church is the only Catholic church in the city of Samarkand, Uzbekistan. It depends on the Apostolic Administration of Uzbekistan based in Tashkent.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St. John the Baptist Church, Samarkand

spots.name: Khoja Doniyor Mausoleum
spots.summary: Khoja Doniyor mausoleum is an architectural monument in Samarkand. It is located in the east side of the Afrosiyab fortress along the Siyob stream. It was built on the grave of Wali Khoja Doniyor. It consists of a rectangular room with a gable and five domes.

spots.name: Oqsaroy
spots.summary: The Oksaroy or Oqsaroy maqbarasi is a fifteenth-century mausoleum in Samarkand, Uzbekistan that served as a burial site for a number of the Timurids. It is located 30 meters southeast of the Gur-e-Amir mausoleum.

spots.name: Shayboni's hut

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Shaybani's hut is an architectural monument of the Middle Ages. The hut in which representatives of the Shaibani Uzbek dynasty were buried is a marble couch. It was built in the 16th century. It is located in Registan Square, Samarkand, Uzbekistan.

spots.name: Amir Burunduk Mausoleum
spots.summary: Amir Burunduk Mausoleum is an architectural monument in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. It was built over the grave of Amir Burunduk, the commander of Amir Temur's army. It is a one-room, gabled, two-story domed building in the Shah-i-Zinda ensemble. The roof was decorated with ceramic rivets, embossed tiles, polished bricks.

spots.name: Unknown Mausoleum-2
spots.summary: Unknown Mausoleum-2 is an architectural monument in Samarkand and is part of the Shah-i-Zinda ensemble. It was built in the 90s of the 14th century. In some sources, the monument was called Ulug Sultanbegi.

spots.name: Ishratkhana Mausoleum
spots.summary: The Ishratkhana Mausoleum is an architectural monument-mausoleum in Samarkand, built during the reign of the Timurid ruler Abu Said (1451-1469). The building, apparently, was the burial place of the female members of the Timurid dynasty, as several female graves were discovered during the excavations in 1940.

spots.name: Unknown Mausoleum-1
spots.summary: Unknown Mausoleum-1 is an architectural monument in Samarkand, part of Shah-i-Zinda ensemble.

spots.name: Shahrisabz Museum of History and Material Culture

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Shahrisabz Museum of History and Material Culture, also known as the Amir Temur Museum of Shahrisabz, is a museum in the city of Shahrisabz, Uzbekistan. It was founded in 1996 on the 660th anniversary of Amir Timur's birth and contains archaeological, ethnographic, and numismatic collections.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Shahrisabz Museum of History and Material Culture

spots.name: Dinamo Samarkand Stadium
spots.summary: Dinamo Stadium is a multi-use stadium in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. It is currently used mostly for football matches and is the home stadium of Dynamo Samarkand.

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Rukhabad Mausoleum
spots.summary: Burial place of the Sufi teacher Burkhan ad-Din Sagardji, who died in the 1380s. It became engulfed by later buildings around Gur-e-Emir, which were cleared away in 1996 so the mausoleum complex was rediscovered and rebuilt.
